input:
A vapour-compression refrigeration unit serves a cold store, evaporating at 0 °C and condensing at 45 °C, which corresponds to a temperature lift across the machine of 45 K. Between these two temperatures, the Carnot coefficient of performance is 6.07. The installed unit, by comparison, achieves a coefficient of performance of 2.75, which is equivalent to 0.45 of the Carnot value.

The Carnot coefficient represents the theoretical ceiling for any vapour-compression machine operating between the same two temperatures. It is based on the assumption of fully reversible operation throughout: no pressure drop in the heat exchangers or lines, no superheat or subcooling penalty, and no losses in the compressor or its motor. The achieved value of 2.75 is taken from the manufacturer's test at full load, and the gap between 2.75 and 6.07 essentially represents the sum of the real losses that the Carnot figure excludes. Expressed as a ratio, the installed unit returns 0.45 of the ideal performance at its test condition, which is really the comparison that the two coefficients exist to make: the ideal value prices the temperature lift, whereas the achieved value prices the lift and the machine together.

It should be noted that the achieved coefficient is stated at full load only. Part-load performance is not stated by the manufacturer, and the coefficient at reduced duty cannot simply be inferred from the full-load figure, so a unit that spends its life operating at part load is not adequately described by 2.75.

The Carnot coefficient is the ceiling for any vapour-compression machine working between the same temperatures. It assumes reversible operation throughout: no pressure drop in the heat exchangers or lines, no superheat or subcooling penalty, and no loss in the compressor or its motor. The achieved value of 2.75 comes from the manufacturer's test at full load, and the distance between 2.75 and 6.07 is the sum of the real losses the Carnot figure excludes. Read as a ratio, the installed unit returns 0.45 of the ideal performance at its test condition, which is the comparison the two coefficients exist to make: the ideal value prices the temperature lift, and the achieved value prices the lift and the machine together.

The achieved coefficient is stated at full load only. Part-load performance is not stated by the manufacturer, and the coefficient at reduced duty cannot be read from the full-load figure or estimated from it by proportion: a unit that spends its working life at part load is simply not described by 2.75.
